review_basis.user_finding: A location-only statistic without team analysis is not a meaningful tactical product; player identity may add inspectable team-event context but must not be presented as proof that a selected training question is correct.
independent_initial_findings: admit only player_id and a normalized shortName-derived display_name
describe the identity as the actor associated with the first recorded follow-up event rather than a receiver or physical first contact
bind event ID, actor, team role, event and sub-event names, offset, selection rule, and join status
keep attribution, transformation notice, and no-endorsement wording visible
reject fallback player labels and fail closed on every missing actor required by the public fixed example
review_basis.independent_final_finding: PASS after 29 source-derived matchup receipts were checked against the raw corner events. Period and source-relative corner time match 29/29, player and event joins remain exact, and the UI time conversion uses period bases 0/45/90/105 with fractional seconds floored. These factual fields improve video lookup without adding contact, marking, weakness, optimal-tactic, or causal inference.

first_recorded_follow_up.selection_rule: earliest event after the corner within the fixed inclusive 10-second window

exact_corroboration.semantic_conclusion: This corroborates the source-linked first recorded follow-up actor only. It does not establish who first touched or received the ball, who won the duel, or whether a tactical decision worked.

time_claim_boundary: PASS — period and source-relative corner time are factual source context only; no receiver, first-contact, marking, weakness, optimal-tactic, or causal inference was added.
